function: Online MIMO-OFDM channel estimation per 5G slot: channel coefficients are NN weights learned via symbol detection on reference signals, tracked by decision-feedback RLS. p. 2, p. 6-7
system: 2x2 MIMO-OFDM, 512 subcarriers, 14 symbols per slot, 3GPP NR scattered reference signals, 2.5 GHz, 7.6 MHz; no RIS. p. 8-9
method: StructNet-CE: channel layer, interference invariant layer and MLP classifier, trained online per slot on reference signals (supervised on pilots, cross-entropy); no offline training. p. 6-7, p. 10
data_channel: QuaDRiGa with 3GPP 3D model (TR 38.901), UMa NLOS, 2.5 GHz, 20 clusters of 20 rays each; user speeds 5 and 30 km/h. p. 9-10, p. 13
test_conditions: Trained online on each slot's reference signals; Eb/No, speed (5, 30 km/h) and modulation varied; offline ReEsNet trained on UMi 1x2, deployed on UMa 2x2. p. 10-11
baselines: Non-learned: LS, empirical LMMSE, decision-directed LS-RLS (also with sphere decoding). Learned: ReEsNet, offline estimator from the authors' earlier work. p. 10-11
metrics: Channel estimation MSE and BER versus Eb/No; CPU run time per slot (Table IV); training time versus MIMO size (Fig. 9). p. 9-12
complexity: Big-O training complexity (Table II) and O(Ns(Nt Ncp)^3) for decision feedback; measured CPU time per slot, 40.24 s for StructNet-CE (Table IV). p. 8, p. 12
openness: none; the paper gives no link to code or data, and the channels come from the QuaDRiGa generator. p. 9
q1_support: p. 9: "realizations are generated by QuaDRiGa" with "The urban macro-cell (UMa) non-line of sight (NLOS) channel scenario is adopted"; the 3GPP 3D model cited as [27] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 13).
q2_support: p. 8: "Initialize the binary classifier weights following normal distribution" (Algorithm 1, inside the loop over slots): StructNet-CE is trained from scratch on each slot, so no trained model is carried to a new condition. The offline-to-online mismatch test on p. 10 ("ReEsNet, is trained offline in the 1 × 2 SIMO-OFDM system") applies only to the baseline.
q3_support: p. 10: "1) LS: the LS solution expressed by eq. (3)" (with em-LMMSE and LS-RLS as further non-learned methods) and "4) ReEsNet: our previous offline learning-based channel estimation approach in [14]"; all are compared on MSE and BER in Figs. 11-13.
q4_support: p. 8: "In this section, we analyze the computational complexity of StructNet-CE" (Big-O in Table II); p. 11: "Table IV presents the CPU run time for processing one 5G slot during the online stage".
q5_support: p. 9: "realizations are generated by QuaDRiGa". QuaDRiGa is a channel generator, not a released dataset; the text and the references give no link or DOI to code or data.
notes: Checked: p. 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TWC.2024.3487111. Area 2 rather than 1: the network detects symbols only to learn the channel, and the main metric is the channel estimation MSE (abstract, p. 1); BER is reported for an LMMSE detector fed with the estimates. q2 judged 0 although the paper claims to avoid the generalization issue, because the method retrains from scratch on every slot; reviewer to confirm. q5 judged 0 because QuaDRiGa is a generator and no release is stated. Table II, III and IV were read from page images (pp. 8 and 12).
